scope: Public aggregate summary only. No full reference inventory, per-specimen inventory, glyph arrays or match coordinates.
method: Same-Unicode nonblank Han comparison against 221 historical BDF references, both whole-cell and cropped-ink exact pixels. CNS1 and CNS2 are disjoint Han sets. Unmapped shape-only matches do not establish character identity.

namedComparisons.name: HP-UX Sung24
namedComparisons.note: The HP24 supplement measured cropped-ink equality only; no whole-cell count is claimed.

isasRelationship.classification: Same-source traditional extension, not an independently new design.

mappingSupplement.method: Original DEC PCF codepoints from preserved recipes remapped according to original Tru64 Chinese documentation: first byte A1–FE; second A1–FE identifies CNS plane 1, second 21–7E identifies plane 2. Transcode those plane coordinates using glibc EUC-TW. No guessing from Unicode-looking code values or source slot indices.
mappingSupplement.note: DEC24/32 use the documented CNS-plane mapping; HP24 was compared separately. These supplements do not fill all historical source and mapping gaps.

sampleOnlySummary.method: Sample-only exact 1-bit cropped-glyph template search in existing public PNGs for same Unicode Han named in each row text. Original AIX CNS1/CNS2 pixels, no scaling or border padding. Search covers complete target PNG; a match is a contained shape, not independently segmented glyph provenance. Nonmatches cannot establish full-font novelty. Alpha>128 and mean RGB<128 define public ink; reference-only photos excluded.
sampleOnlySummary.interpretation: Only isolated common-character shape matches were found; this sample-only search is not a complete-source font comparison.

limits: 49 current IDs were absent from the old BDF archive; mapped HP24 was supplemented separately. Other missing or unmapped full sources remain gaps. Withdrawn references are included only where historical source data exists; no withdrawn PNGs were recovered. Sporadic same-Unicode sample-shape matches are not whole-sentence or whole-font duplication, and nonmatches do not establish originality.
